sentenceSets.sentence: She served as the principal interlocutor for the negotiations, a role that required equal parts patience and authority.

answerChoices.reasoning: A mediator draws influence from having no stake and belonging to neither side, but the sentence says the role carried authority, which means she spoke on someone's behalf.
An arbiter decides the matter and imposes the result, which would make the patience the sentence stresses unnecessary.
An envoy is dispatched somewhere to deliver a position and return, while the sentence describes a standing place inside the negotiations themselves.
A liaison keeps two organizations informed of each other, a coordinating job that would not demand the authority the sentence attaches to the role.
A delegate is one of several sent to represent a body, whereas the sentence singles her out as the principal one.
An advocate argues a case to a decision-maker, but a negotiation has no judge to persuade—only the other side to keep talking to.
A translator carries words between languages and would need neither the authority nor the standing the sentence describes.
A moderator manages a discussion without taking part in its substance, which does not fit someone whose job requires authority of her own.
A bystander takes no part at all, which contradicts her serving in a principal role.
An adversary is who she faced across the table, not the position she occupied.
An archivist keeps records and has no function in a live negotiation.

sentenceSets.sentence: In the dialogue Socrates chooses an interlocutor who is confident enough to keep answering and unwary enough to contradict himself.

answerChoices.reasoning: Opponent frames the exchange as a contest to be won, but the man is chosen for his willingness to keep answering, which is what sustains a conversation rather than a fight.
A pupil is there to be taught, while this man is selected for his confidence in asserting things of his own.
Respondent belongs to formal proceedings where one party answers a charge, and the sentence describes an informal give-and-take of questions and replies.
A foil is defined by the contrast it throws on someone else, which names a literary function rather than the man's part in the talking.
A disciple already accepts the teacher's views and so would have little to contradict himself about.
A critic evaluates from outside, but this man is inside the exchange, supplying the answers Socrates works with.
Rival implies competition for the same standing or prize, and nothing in the sentence suggests the two want the same thing.
A witness reports what he has seen, whereas this man is being drawn into stating positions he then undermines.
A narrator tells the story from outside it and would not be chosen by a character within the dialogue.
A spectator watches silently, which cannot be squared with someone who keeps answering.
A scribe writes down what is said rather than taking a part in saying it.

sentenceSets.sentence: The chatbot's designers trained it to mirror whatever register its interlocutor used, which made long conversations feel oddly circular.

answerChoices.reasoning: User names anyone who operates the software, but what the system copies is specifically the speech of the person talking with it.
A correspondent exchanges letters or messages across a distance, while the sentence describes conversations sustained long enough to start doubling back on themselves.
An operator runs a machine, and a register is something a person adopts in speaking rather than a control that gets worked.
An audience receives without speaking, yet the mirroring described depends entirely on the other party producing language of their own.
Client marks a commercial relationship, which has no bearing on whose manner of speech the system imitates.
A subscriber is someone who pays for access, a billing category rather than a participant in the exchange being described.
The programmers are the designers named earlier in the sentence, not the party whose register is copied during a conversation.
A listener supplies nothing to copy, and the circularity arises because the system feeds a person's own manner back at them.
A manufacturer builds the product and does not appear in the conversation at all.
A regulator oversees an industry and has no role in the exchange the sentence describes.
A vendor sells the software rather than talking with it.
